record.paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
record.original_question: For a fixed affine Poisson manifold (M^r_aff,P), how many of the countably many universal symmetries obtained by applying O→r to wheel cocycles and their iterated commutators in ker d are globally nonzero sections of Λ^2TM^r_aff rather than vanishing identically?

evidence.quote: Problem 14. For a given affine Poisson manifold (M^r_aff,P), how many universal symmetries – taken from the countable set O→r(γ ∈ ker d)(P) produced by the graph orientation morphism O→r from the grt-related wheel cocycles and their iterated commutators [14, 29] – do not vanish identically as global sections from Γ(Λ^2TM^r_aff) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}$ denote a finite-dimensional affine real manifold of dimension $r$, equipped with a Poisson bivector $P\in\Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}})$. Let $\mathsf{GC}_2$ be the Kontsevich graph complex of undirected graphs (with the differential $d$ given by vertex expansion), and let $\ker d\subset\mathsf{GC}_2$ be the space of graph cocycles. The Lie subalgebra $\mathfrak{grt}$ of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra is known (by Willwacher's theorem) to embed into $H^0(\mathsf{GC}_2)$, and contains an infinite family of cocycles built from the $(2\ell+1)$-wheel graphs (for $\ell\geq 1$) together with all iterated Lie brackets thereof; this yields a countable family $\{\gamma_i\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}}\subset\ker d$.

Let $\mathcal{O}\vec{r}\colon\mathsf{GC}_2\to\mathrm{End}(\text{Poisson bivectors})$ denote the Kontsevich orientation morphism: for a graph cocycle $\gamma$ on $n$ vertices and $2n-2$ edges, $\mathcal{O}\vec{r}(\gamma)(P)$ is the formal sum, over all admissible orientations in which each of the $n$ original vertices is the tail of exactly two arrows, of the bivector obtained by inserting copies of $P$ at the vertices and contracting along edges. The output $\mathcal{O}\vec{r}(\gamma)(P)\in\Gamma(\Lambda^2 TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}})$ is a universal infinitesimal symmetry of the Poisson structure $P$.

Question. For a fixed affine Poisson manifold $(M^r_{\mathrm{aff}},P)$, determine how many elements of the countable family $\{\mathcal{O}\vec{r}(\gamma_i)(P)\}_{i\in\mathbb{N}}$ are nonzero as global sections of $\Lambda^2 TM^r_{\mathrm{aff}}$, i.e. do not vanish identically on $M^r_{\mathrm{aff}}$.
artifact.category_tag: Kontsevich graph complex and Poisson geometry
artifact.status_search_result: The orientation morphism from graph cocycles to Poisson symmetries is actively studied (Buring–Kiselev–Rutten and others). Tetrahedron, pentagon-wheel, and heptagon-wheel cocycles are explicitly known to produce nontrivial symmetries in specific cases, but no general count of how many of the countably many wheel-and-iterated-bracket symmetries are globally nonvanishing on a given affine Poisson manifold appears in the literature; the question remains open.

status_evidence.title: The Kontsevich graph orientation morphism revisited
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses orientation morphism producing infinitesimal symmetries of Poisson brackets from graph cocycles.
status_evidence.claim: The orientation morphism construction is the object of ongoing study; questions about (non)triviality of resulting symmetries remain open.

status_evidence.title: The heptagon-wheel cocycle in the Kontsevich graph complex
status_evidence.snippet: Heptagon-wheel cocycle built of 46 graphs on 8 vertices and 14 edges; tetrahedron and pentagon-wheel were previously known solutions.
status_evidence.claim: Only finitely many wheel cocycles are explicitly constructed; the global nontriviality of the full countable family of induced symmetries on a fixed affine Poisson manifold is not established.

status_evidence.title: Universal Cocycles and the Graph Complex Action on Homogeneous Poisson Brackets
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the action of graph complex cocycles on Poisson brackets in specific homogeneous settings.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on nonvanishing exist for special Poisson structures but no general counting answer.
